transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC · 42 minutes · Maya Patel, Ethan Liu, Carlos Vega; Karen Park, Ravi Menon, Lena Ortiz, Samir Gupta

Summary: quick sync on pilot onboarding and infra readiness. A few transcription artifacts present, informal style.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 42 minutes, so we'll run through status and then dig into the perf numbers Ethan put together.
[00:18] Karen Park: Thanks Maya, appreciate it. Morning for us in EST, I think. We got Ravi and Lena on.
[00:26] Ravi Menon: Yep hi all.
[00:28] Lena Ortiz: Hi.
[00:30] Ethan Liu: Alright, quick agenda: onboarding checklist, access and VPC peering, initial results from hosted pilot, tuning suggestions, and open questions especially around security.
[00:40] Maya Patel: Cool. First item, onboarding: Lena, you were going to confirm the VPC peering and service account access last week, where are we at?
[00:50] Lena Ortiz: We did the initial peering test, but there was a firewall port issue, we need to open 443 and 10250 for the agent. I put the notes in the ticket but haven't finalized the peering CIDR whitelist. Also, our infra team wants to use SAML SSO for console access, so we'll need the SAML metadata from Redwood.
[01:12] Maya Patel: Got it. We'll send the SAML metadata and a step-by-step for console SSO. Ethan, can you call out what ports and IP ranges we need documented for the private control plane?
[01:22] Ethan Liu: Sure, I'll include a concise list in the follow-up email. For the hosted pilot we just needed API key and token, but for the private we need VPC peering, route tables updated, and specific egress rules. Note, some of those were auto detected by our agent but it's best if Lena shares the exact CIDR.
[01:45] Lena Ortiz: Yeah I'll share that after the call.
[01:48] Maya Patel: Great. Next, access: Ravi, were you able to run the initial inference set we provided?
[01:55] Ravi Menon: I ran the set, we got consistent responses but latency varied. For the 512-token prompts we saw median latency about 220ms per token for the hosted API, but end-to-end request latency was around 420ms, which is a bit higher than we expected. I'm not sure if the client batching is happening right.
[02:18] Ethan Liu: When you say 220ms per token, do you mean per-token model time or overall? Might be a transcription. Usually per-token is lower; sounds like end-to-end. Can you share the exact test harness results?
[02:30] Ravi Menon: Yeah I'll upload the harness CSV. I noticed the batch size in the client was at 1, we can try increasing it to 4 or 8 to see throughput gains. Also, I think the KV-cache wasn't enabled in the initial run so we lost prefix speedups.
[02:47] Carlos Vega: Quick note, KV cache has to be enabled in the runtime flags, sometimes the client lib defaults off in earlier SDK versions.
[02:56] Maya Patel: Ethan, do you have the pilot numbers you prepared?
[03:00] Ethan Liu: Yup, I uploaded a short spreadsheet to the shared drive (link in chat). High level: hosted baseline with openai-ish sized model (Redwood-curated 7B variant) — median request latency 380ms, p95 ~720ms on the default config. With batching tuned to 4 we saw throughput improvement of about 1.8x, latency p95 moved to ~640ms. On dedicated cores (small Dedicated pool) we got p95 down to ~420ms. Note these are early and noisy.
[03:34] Karen Park: Can you repeat the model names? Redwood-curated 7B, is that quantized?
[03:40] Ethan Liu: It's the 7B float model initially, not quantized. We ran a q4_0 profile in a follow-up run — quantized model dropped memory and improved throughput but some low-rate output differences, nothing major but Ravi, you should validate output quality.
[03:56] Ravi Menon: I did a quick diff, most outputs were fine but occasionally truncation and slightly changed tokenization around medical abbreviations — needs a closer check.
[04:08] Maya Patel: That's expected; we'll add quantization guidance. Our Optimize team suggests q4_0 for throughput but q8_0 or per-layer mixed quant for higher QA. We'll send recommended configs.
[04:20] Samir Gupta: On the security side, I'm still concerned about encryption at rest and key management. Who holds the keys in hosted pilot?
[04:28] Carlos Vega: By default for hosted AP I think Redwood manages the keys, but for Dedicated or Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. Might have been mis-transcribed but we do have KMS integration.
[04:40] Maya Patel: Correct — hosted uses Redwood-managed keys unless you enable BYOK. For Private we can integrate with your KMS. We'll attach SOC2 and KMS integration docs after the call.
[04:52] Samir Gupta: Please include whether logs can be routed to our SIEM and retention windows.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Will do.
[05:00] Ethan Liu: Back to perf tuning — two levers: batching (client-side) and runtime batching. Also prefix caching (KV cache) for repeated conversation prefixes. For large prompt workloads, continuous batching helps a lot but adds tail latency. If low tail latency is critical, you might want a dedicated pool.
[05:25] Karen Park: Our SLO is p95 under 500ms for chat flows, and 300ms for short completions. Is that realistic on hosted?
[05:33] Ethan Liu: Hosted can hit that for short completions with a smaller model and aggressive quantization; for chat flows with 512 tokens it's tight. Dedicated pool with pinned capacity is the safer route. There's a cost trade-off.
[05:46] Ravi Menon: Cost question: how much delta between hosted and a small dedicated cluster? We have a ballpark budget.
[05:52] Maya Patel: We'll include ballpark numbers in the pricing spreadsheet. For many customers, dedicated is roughly 2-4x hosted costs depending on commit and utilization, but gives the latency guarantees.
[06:06] Lena Ortiz: Another infra item: our compliance team needs audit logs for admin actions and API calls. Are those available by default?
[06:14] Carlos Vega: We provide audit logs for Dedicated and Private with retention options. Hosted has limited audit metadata but we can provide expanded logs as an add-on. We'll document specifics.
[06:24] Samir Gupta: Also SAML SSO integration for our engineers — we need the ACS URL and metadata xml.
[06:30] Maya Patel: We'll send the SAML metadata and a quick guide.
[06:33] Karen Park: On the data residency note: some of our PHI data must remain in us-east-1 and not cross regions. Is Redwood able to pin region?
[06:43] Ethan Liu: For Dedicated and Private yes; hosted we can route to a region but cannot guarantee data doesn't traverse. For strict residency you want Dedicated or Private in your desired region.
[06:56] Ravi Menon: Good to know.
[07:00] Maya Patel: Let's go over next steps from the pilot test and what we need from Nexa to make the environment ready for a more robust run. Ethan?
[07:08] Ethan Liu: Actionable items: 1) Enable KV cache and re-run the harness with batching at 4 and 8, capture p50/p95/p99; 2) Try q4_0 and q8_0 runs and capture output diffs; 3) We'll give a script to simulate 50rps and 200rps to measure autoscale behavior. I've uploaded the harness, but I'll also push a Dockerized runner.
[07:36] Ravi Menon: Sounds good, I'll run the Dockerized runner on our side once Lena confirms peering.
[07:42] Lena Ortiz: I'll schedule the firewall change and share the CIDR by EOD Tuesday.
[07:48] Maya Patel: Perfect. On the quality front, can we define a small eval set — Ravi mentioned 1k prompts — if you can add expected outputs that helps us quantify regressions.
[07:58] Ravi Menon: I'll prepare 1k prompts with target snippets and a small scorer.
[08:04] Carlos Vega: We'll run our automated regression tool and flag hallucinations and tokenization mismatches. Also note that some medical tokens are non-standard; we recommend providing a custom tokenizer or post-processing rules if necessary.
[08:20] Karen Park: Re: hallucinations, what's your recommended threshold for pilot acceptance?
[08:25] Ethan Liu: Typically <2% critical hallucination rate on the eval set for production, but for pilot we accept up to 5% while we tune. We'll capture examples.
[08:35] Samir Gupta: For compliance, please include data deletion guarantees in the SOW if we test with PHI.
[08:42] Maya Patel: We'll add a clause and sample SOW language.
[08:47] Karen Park: One more question — how do model rollouts and A/B tests work in Redwood? We want canary deploys and quick rollback.
[08:55] Ethan Liu: We support canary and A/B rollouts at the route level. You can pin traffic percentages to model variants, and Redwood Console shows per-variant metrics and allows auto-fallback to a safe variant on errors or quality regressions. There's also an audit trail for rollouts.
[09:12] Ravi Menon: Great.
[09:15] Maya Patel: Alright, let's do a quick review of the action items and owners — I'll read them out. Maya to send pricing/SP and SAML metadata by Monday; Ethan to send harness + Docker runner and quant guide; Lena to confirm CIDR and open firewall ports; Ravi to deliver sample prompts and output expectations; Samir to review SOC2 docs and list extra asks. Everyone ok?
[09:34] Karen Park: Yup.
[09:35] Lena Ortiz: OK.
[09:36] Samir Gupta: Sounds good.
[09:37] Ethan Liu: I'll also attach the spreadsheet with the baseline numbers and the link in the follow-up.
[09:42] Maya Patel: Anything else? This is probably a small question: competitor ask — Karen had mentioned Bedrock and Anthropic, do you want us to outline why Redwood vs those?
[09:50] Karen Park: It would be helpful — specifically around latency guarantees and private deployment story.
[09:56] Maya Patel: We'll include a short comparison doc.
[09:59] Ravi Menon: One minor transcript glitch I remember — the SDK version we used was 1.2.0, earlier SDKs had KV cache disabled by default.
[10:08] Carlos Vega: Yep, SDK 1.2.1 and later have KV cache opt-in flipped to true in the default config, but we'll include explicit runtime flag in the script.
[10:18] Maya Patel: Ok great. We'll follow up with the items and set the infra deep dive for next week. Thanks everyone.
[10:26] Karen Park: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:28] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-heard words and shorthand (e.g., 'q4_0' typed sometimes as 'q forty'). References to internal docs and shared drive are present as links in chat (not reproduced here).
